input_sentence: SpaceX went public with its IPO priced at $135 per share.
headline: SpaceX Goes Public: Largest IPO in History at $135 Per Share
dek: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. raised $75 billion on Nasdaq under ticker SPCX, smashing every prior IPO record and setting up Elon Musk to become the world's first trillionaire.
summary: SpaceX priced its IPO at $135 per share for 555.6 million Class A shares on the night of June 11, 2026, raising approximately $75 billion — the largest IPO in U.S. history, more than tripling Saudi Aramco's prior record of $24.9 billion. The $SPCX ticker went live on the Nasdaq Global Select Market and Nasdaq Texas on June 12, 2026. Total investor demand exceeded $250 billion, roughly 3.5–4x oversubscribed, with retail orders alone topping $100 billion. At the IPO price, SpaceX is valued at approximately $1.77 trillion, and Musk retains about 82% of voting power through a dual-class share structure.

timeline.label: SpaceX founded
timeline.description: Elon Musk founded Space Exploration Technologies Corp. with the goal of reducing space launch costs and colonizing Mars.

timeline.label: SpaceX acquires xAI and X
timeline.description: SpaceX bought xAI — Musk's AI company that owns X (formerly Twitter) — in an all-stock deal valued at ~$250 billion; xAI later rebranded as SpaceXAI.

timeline.label: S-1 filing made public
timeline.description: SpaceX's IPO registration statement (S-1) became publicly available, disclosing financials and plans to sell ~555.6 million shares at $135 per share.

timeline.label: Retail indication-of-interest window closes
timeline.description: Fidelity and other participating brokers closed their retail investor indication-of-interest windows at 4:00 PM ET.

timeline.label: IPO officially priced at $135
timeline.description: SpaceX confirmed the final IPO price of $135 per share, raising ~$75 billion. Retail orders had already exceeded $100 billion.

timeline.label: $SPCX begins trading on Nasdaq
timeline.description: SpaceX shares went live on the Nasdaq Global Select Market and Nasdaq Texas under ticker SPCX, marking the historic public debut.

timeline.label: Expected offering close
timeline.description: The IPO is expected to formally close, subject to standard conditions. Underwriters have 30 days from this date to exercise their option for 83.3 million additional shares.

why_it_matters: SpaceX's IPO is the largest in U.S. history, more than tripling Saudi Aramco's prior record, and signals a new era of private space infrastructure entering public markets. With Starlink serving 10 million customers across 160 countries and Starship still scaling, quarterly earnings scrutiny will for the first time expose the financial trajectory of the world's dominant launch provider. The deal also raises profound governance questions — Musk's 82% voting control, mandatory arbitration clauses, and Texas corporate law give shareholders unusually limited recourse, setting a precedent that regulators and index-fund investors will be watching closely.

extras.rollout_status: Shares went live on Nasdaq Global Select Market and Nasdaq Texas on June 12, 2026. Up to 30% of shares (~$23 billion) reserved for retail investors via brokers including Fidelity. Offering expected to close June 15, 2026. Underwriters hold a 30-day option to purchase an additional 83.3 million shares.

reactions.take: In a 12-page letter to SEC Commissioner Paul Atkins, Warren requested a delay of the IPO, arguing SpaceX's governance structure gives Musk 'unprecedented level of power' over investors, that mandatory arbitration guts shareholder rights, and that analysts have called the valuation 'nonsensical' and 'smoke-and-mirrors accounting.' She also warned that passive index-fund investors could be forced into SpaceX exposure with no choice.

reactions.source: Ann Lipton, law professor, University of Colorado Boulder
reactions.take: Told the Wall Street Journal that SpaceX is 'essentially closing off every possible avenue for shareholders to have any influence at all,' citing the combination of supervoting shares, mandatory arbitration, stricter rules on shareholder proposals, and Texas corporate law.
Called the IPO 'the most ambitious mission in human history' opening to ordinary investors, noting that through the offering, millions of people now hold a piece of SpaceX, xAI, and X simultaneously.
Noted that millions of retail investors now hold a piece of all three Musk ventures — SpaceX, xAI, and X — via the single public offering.
Priced synthetic SpaceX shares at $167 ahead of the debut, implying market participants expected roughly a 24% first-day pop from the $135 IPO price.
Retail sentiment around $SPCX was rated 'extremely bullish' on the platform heading into the debut.
Placed an order to purchase at least $5 billion in SpaceX shares ahead of the IPO — nearly as much as the entire $5.5 billion Cerebras IPO earlier in 2026.

Cautioned that 'space is hard' — the industry is capital-intensive, delays are common, and outright failures happen — urging investors to weigh SpaceX's extraordinary engineering ambitions against very real execution risk.

whats_next: First-day trading performance of $SPCX on June 12 — whether the stock pops toward the $167 Hyperliquid synthetic price or trades near the $135 IPO price.
Potential exercise of the underwriters' 30-day option to purchase an additional 83.3 million shares, which would raise a further ~$11 billion.
SpaceX's first quarterly earnings call as a public company — bringing Starlink growth, Starship commercial launches, and government contract revenue under public scrutiny for the first time.
Google GPU deal begins October 2026: $920 million/month contract will be a closely watched revenue line item.
Potential regulatory follow-up from the SEC following Sen. Warren's letter requesting a review of governance disclosures and index-fund exposure.
